key_insight: This paper reframes reward supervision by using rubrics to guide self-distillation, reducing dependence on expensive chain-of-thought annotations and noisy rationales. The core idea is to turn evaluative feedback into a structured teaching signal that better aligns reasoning models during post-training.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between high-quality final answers and low-quality reasoning traces in supervised distillation, as well as the limitations of reward feedback that is too compressed or hard to learn from effectively.
method: Condition self-distillation on rubrics so the model learns from structured evaluation criteria rather than only raw rationales.
Use rubric-based supervision to make post-training signals more informative, stable, and less dependent on manually written chain-of-thought annotations.
Bridge supervised distillation and reward-based training by converting feedback into a clearer, reusable training target.
impact: For AI practitioners, this can lower annotation cost while improving the quality of reasoning supervision. It may lead to more reliable and scalable post-training pipelines for reasoning models.
